title: Introduce fleet spillover reservation broker and soft throughput fence
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Fleet autoscalers and reservation systems handle most sustained load patterns well, but we still see short cross-pool contention events where tenants briefly exceed their committed throughput and trigger noisy evictions or emergency preempts. Those events drive user-visible latency spikes and reduce overall utilization due to conservative warm pool sizing. This PR introduces a Spillover Reservation Broker (SRB) and a soft throughput fence concept to probabilistically absorb transient over-supply without immediate hard preemption. Summary: 1) Controller: new controller that tracks per-pool committed reservations, short-term spillover demand, and a tunable soft fence margin. 2) Admission path integration: lightweight admission-side check that consults SRB to decide whether to admit requests into ephemeral spillover capacity. 3) Rebalancer: periodic background reconciler that redistributes ephemeral reservations back to pools with sustained need. 4) Telemetry: adds srb.* metrics (spill_rate, ephemeral_usage, fence_violations, reservation_leak_estimate) and dashboards. 5) Safety and controls: feature-flagged behind feature.alpha.srb, config knobs for margin (percentage), max-ephemeral-per-pool, and leak-back window. 6) Tests: unit tests for controller logic, e2e scenario harness that simulates inter-pool spikes, and chaos test that validates graceful degradation with node drain. Goals and outcomes: The SRB is intended to: - reduce hard preemptions for transient spikes - increase overall cluster utilization by allowing short lived oversubscription - keep SLA degradation bounded via soft fences and probabilistic shedding Implementation notes: - The broker uses an exponential smoothing window (90s) to classify transient vs sustained demand and a randomized admission probability when ephemeral headroom is low. - Rebalancer reclaims ephemeral reservations gradually (configurable 'leak-back' half-life) to avoid oscillations. - Admission decision is O(1) and avoids blocking the serving hot path; a cached token bucket in each gateway reduces RPCs to the controller. Performance summary from canary: - On synthetic cross-pool spike workload (10 tenants, 20s spike): 67% fewer emergency preempts, 6.4% drop in p95 latency violations, and 11.8% cluster utilization improvement in steady-state follow-up. - Median admission decision latency added: ~120us (cached fast-path) in the API gateway. Checklist: - [x] Controller implementation and CRD-like config structure - [x] Admission-side integration and cached token path - [x] Rebalancer and leak-back policy - [x] Telemetry + Grafana dashboard panels - [x] Feature flag + config knobs - [x] Unit + integration + chaos tests - [x] Docs: design doc and operation notes (internal) Rollout plan: Start behind feature.alpha.srb in main clusters with conservative defaults (margin=12%, max-ephemeral-per-pool=8%). Monitor srb.spill_rate and fence_violations; promote to broader clusters after 2 weeks of stable metrics and no elevated SLA regressions. Related: ENG-2314 (fleet contention investigation), SUP-4421 (customer incident that motivated spillover path).

release_notes: Introduce experimental Spillover Reservation Broker (SRB) to absorb short transient overages without hard preemption. Feature-flagged and off by default. Provides srb.* metrics and dashboards. Improves utilization and reduces emergency preempts in cross-pool spike scenarios.
monitoring_playbook: Monitor srb.spill_rate, srb.fence_violations, and per-pool ephemeral_usage. If fence_violations > 0.5% sustained for 5m, roll back by disabling feature.alpha.srb or lowering max-ephemeral-per-pool.
